key_insight: Photovoltaics look energetically strong at the panel level, but their net energy advantage shrinks sharply once reliable, around-the-clock electricity delivery and firming are included.
engineering_relevance: For power-system design, the study shows that storage, overbuild, backup, and fuel supply can dominate lifecycle energy and emissions, so decarbonization targets must be evaluated at the grid-delivery level, not just the device level.
method: Fleet-equivalent benchmark model, not a simulation or optimization
Compares unfirmed renewable supply against battery, hydrogen, and gas-firmed delivery
Uses an illustrative Central European mix of 80% wind and 20% PV with lifecycle EROI and GWP100 accounting
evidence_signal: The abstract reports EROI falling from 10.7–16.0 unfirmed to 0.7–2.3 with 24 h battery balancing, 3.4–7.7 for seasonal hydrogen, and GWP100 rising from 38–75 to 80–289 gCO2eq/kWh for firmed systems.
watch_item: The benchmark uses favorable accounting assumptions and illustrative mixes, so real deployments with non-unity orientation, site, curtailment, and delivery factors will likely perform worse.
paper_title: Photovoltaics beyond the panel: system-level net energy under grid and firming constraints
